- **Deduplicated `customers_n` view** (normalized by name/email): 304 distinct customer identities, with a `duplicates` column that sums to 316, exactly matching the raw row count.

The gap (316 vs 304) is 12 ambiguous duplicate pairs. In each case, the same person appears twice with the same email but different letter case (e.g. `ana.park14@example.com` vs `ANA.PARK14@EXAMPLE.COM`), a different `cust_id`, and the duplicate record missing a phone number and having no matching transactions in `pos_sales` (only the original lowercase-email `cust_id` has sales activity, e.g. cust_0010 has 21 sales lines while its duplicate cust_0300 has none). Names affected: Ana Park, Ben Park, Cara Park, Dev Park, Eli Park, Fay Park, Gus Park, Hana Park, Kai Ruiz, Lea Ruiz, Mo Ruiz, Nia Ruiz.

So the business has 304 real distinct customers, with 12 of them double-counted in the raw table due to case-sensitive email duplication (24 rows involved, 12 excess/ambiguous rows). No other ambiguity (e.g. same email different case with real differing data) was found beyond this pattern.

No other ambiguous records were found.
